claim: The adapter can hand the wrong reference to the writer (Cref = span, or Bref = mean chord) and every fast test passes. claim: The section of a body at an inserted station can ignore the taper (half-width taken from the lower neighbour instead of interpolated) without a failure: every parent and canopy of the tests has constant a, b, n and centre along x. A real fuselage tapers, so the merged body's width at every canopy station, its area for the AVL body radius and its wetted area would be wrong.
evidence: assert [s.xyz[0] for s in found.x_secs] == [0.0, 0.3, 0.5, 0.6, 1.0]  -- the only assert on inserted stations is their x; fuselage_box() is [section(0.0, 0.05, 0.04), section(0.5, 0.05, 0.04), section(1.0, 0.05, 0.04)].
recommended_test: Fast, test_solver_bodies.py: parent body([section(0.0, 0.02, 0.02, z=0.0), section(1.0, 0.06, 0.04, z=0.02)]) and a narrow canopy far above it, body([section(0.25, 0.01, 0.01, z=0.2), section(0.75, 0.01, 0.01, z=0.2)], 'canopy', 'Rumpf'). The canopy is narrower than the parent, so the merged half-width is the interpolated parent's: at x = 0.25 a = 0.02 + 0.25*0.04 = 0.03 and the bottom z - b = 0.005 - 0.025 = -0.02; at x = 0.75 a = 0.05, bottom 0.015 - 0.035 = -0.02. Assert station.a (rel 1e-6) and station.xyz[2] - station.b (abs 1e-9) at both inserted stations (the unmutated code returns exactly these). A second case with n = 2 at one parent section and n = 4 at the next pins the interpolation of the exponents through the area of the parent-only half.
